 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Three straight losses usually cost a team the benefit of the doubt. The Carolina Panthers apparently kept some of it, because the national experts like Bryce Young and company to leave the Superdome with sole possession of first place in the NFC South.
 Both teams are 3-5, and the Saints are 1.5-point favorites at home. By our count, 15 of the 22 panelists at ESPN, NFL.com and Sports Illustrated picked Carolina anyway.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement NFL.com is 4-1 for Carolina
 Oct 4, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young (9) drops back to pass defended by offensive tackle Monroe Freeling (57), guard Robert Hunt (50) and center Luke Fortner (77) during the first half at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images
 Jeremy Bergman (24-21), Brooke Cersosimo (26-23), Bobby Kownack (30-27) and Dan Parr (24-22) all took the Panthers in NFL.com's weekly picks. Gennaro Filice was the lone Saints vote at 21-20, and he called it "a matchup between underwhelming division rivals."
 Kownack's 30-27 projection was the highest-scoring of the group, and it fits what Young did last week. He threw for 276 yards and three touchdowns in the 26-21 loss to Denver .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement ESPN goes 5-2 for the Panthers
 Matt Bowen, Dan Graziano, Kalyn Kahler, Pamela Maldonado and Jason Reid picked Carolina on ESPN's panel. Mike Clay and Eric Moody went with New Orleans.
 The ESPN lean makes sense when you look at the Saints' injuries up front. New Orleans will be without center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga, and Derrick Brown gets a backup center making his first start.
 SI's panel is the closest
 Nov 8, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Carolina Panthers wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (4) celebrates with guard Robert Hunt (50) after scoring a touchdown against the Denver Broncos during the second half at Bank of America Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images
 Sports Illustrated's 10 experts split 6-4 for Carolina . Albert Breer, Eva Geitheim, Mitch Goldich, Conor Orr, Iain MacMillan and Peter Dewey took the Panthers, while Mike Kadlick, Gilberto Manzano, John Pluym and Matt Verderame picked the Saints.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The reason for caution is Carolina's protection. Young has been sacked 26 times in eight games, and the Panthers have an offensive line problem heading into a game against Chase Young and Carl Granderson, who have combined for 15.5 sacks. If the line holds up, the experts who picked Carolina will look smart, and Dave Canales gets a little breathing room .
